title: HC Mike LaFleur Press Conference: October 30 | Week 8 vs. Dallas Cowboys
headline: Jeremiyah Love is expected to return from a two-week ankle absence and play Sunday vs. Dallas; the OL is shaky, with Jon Gaines out and Hjalte Froholdt limited.
summary: LaFleur opened by saying Jon Gaines is out for the game; the caption also names a second player who is out, but the name is garbled. He said the run game has improved since the muddy-run discussion but still has a long way to go, and he framed it as a matter of mindset and continuity with a shuffled group of linemen. Jeremiyah Love is expected to play Sunday after missing two weeks with an ankle injury. LaFleur said no one is truly at 100% by November 1st and that Love feels as good as he can, and he stressed that a back has to be dynamic when planting and cutting. Elijah Wilkinson should be full today, and LaFleur said a rib issue is only a matter of pain tolerance. Hjalte Froholdt was limited after a minor tweak and will be monitored through Saturday. Hayden Conner would be the backup center, and LaFleur praised new tackle Jedrick Wills Jr.'s demeanor and said he is positioned to be ready if called on. LaFleur also said new WR Zay Jones is catching the ball well while running with the look squad. He called the red zone a point of emphasis and said he has to find a way to score more touchdowns. The rest was a general discussion of linebacker value.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski Week 8 Media Availability | Friday, October 30th | Press Conference
headline: Defensive rookies Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins are praised as early-career starters, and James Pierce is set to return to the 53-man roster and play next week. Pierce is not on the provided roster, so no signal is attached to him.
summary: Stefanski opened with a question about a player's hand or arm injury, joked about the 'Thanos' club and said the player has played with a similar cast in the past. His answer was 'we'll see', so the status is unclear and the player is not identified. He called C.J. Henderson very valuable schematically and said he has been playing well. He praised rookies Kendal Daniels and Harold Perkins as day-three picks who are already playing like starters and handling extra versatility, and he credited the players first and the staff second. He confirmed the team plans to activate James Pierce to the 53-man roster next week, that Pierce will travel to Madrid, and that the plan is for him to play next week. He added that Pierce will be a positive addition to the pass rush plan. He had no update on Ontario Thompson's designation. The rest of the session covered red zone philosophy (Fridays are red zone day, defenses change play calls around the 11-yard line, and it is harder to find windows in the run game), the hook-and-lateral trick play, Madrid travel planning, and his own growth as a head coach.

The travel schedule was set collaboratively after studying how other teams handled international trips, and Stefanski is comfortable with the plan.

title: Jesse Minter Announces Lamar Jackson's Return
headline: Lamar Jackson expected to return this week vs. Buffalo after a full practice week; Vega Ioane has a chance but is still undecided.
summary: Coach Minter opened by saying the team expects Lamar Jackson to play this week, and that Jackson likely showed as a full participant in all three practices. He credited Jackson for his work rehabbing the injury and said he expects Jackson to look like his usual self, playing his own style of football and not being a 'statue.' Minter said Jackson's return gives the team an energy jolt, but he also said the team should not lean on Jackson as a crutch. He praised the backup QB (called 'Snoop', most likely Tyler Huntley) for putting the team in position to win most of the last three games. On guard Vega Ioane, Minter said he has put in work to potentially play and the decision would come in the next couple of hours, with the injury report to follow. Asked about Jaylinn Hawkins, he said flatly that Hawkins will be out this week. The opponent is Buffalo, which Minter called a really good team in a really good environment.

title: Joe Brady Addresses Bills Injury Updates, Starting Safety, And Challenges In Facing The Baltimore Ravens
headline: Damar Hamlin starts at safety vs. Baltimore, but TE Dalton Kincaid, WR DJ Moore and LT Spencer Brown are all questionable and WR Tyrell Shavers is out.
summary: Brady opened with the injury report: Kincaid, DJ Moore, Spencer Brown, Dee Alford and Greg Gaines are questionable, and Tyrell Shavers is out. He said someone tweaked a lower body in practice today, without making clear who. He said he trusts Brown to play without a full practice week because of his experience, his preparation and his high level of play. Brady said the team used the bye well, had three strong practice days, and showed good attention to detail after the self-scout. Damar Hamlin will start at safety. Brady praised his versatility, said he has played nickel without hesitation in the past, and said he has earned the larger role. If Alford can't play, Brady gave no specific nickel plan beyond saying several players can move inside or outside. He called the Ravens' defense different from past Baltimore units because new head coach Jesse Minter brings the scheme he ran at Michigan and with the Chargers, combined with Anthony Weaver, whose Dolphins defense did well against Buffalo last year. He also said Baltimore will bring the best version of Lamar Jackson, and that the Bills will have their hands full with Zay Flowers.

title: Dave Canales addresses defensive coaching changes
headline: Panthers fired DC Ejiro Evero and another defensive coach; Todd Wash takes over as interim play-caller, and the offense still needs to fix its protection issues. CB Will Lee has a hamstring injury with no timeline yet.
summary: Canales opened by announcing the dismissals of defensive coordinator EJ Ibarra and Jonathan Cooley. He said the decision was his, made after gathering information over time and weighing the games remaining and the team's spot in the division. Todd Wash will take over the defense and call it from here on out. Canales praised Wash's experience, his understanding of front and run-game mechanics, and his connection with the players. He wants the defense to play fast, physical and connected, starting with the run game and owning first and second down. Staff roles are being reshuffled: Renaldo Hill takes over the secondary and A.C. Carter moves to the front and defensive tackles. On offense, he acknowledged that opponents are now taking away the vertical passing game and that protection has been inconsistent. He said the offense needs a more rhythmic, balanced approach and a better run game. He said the line has to be clean at the snap to give Bryce Young time. Will Lee's hamstring injury and the offensive line injuries were discussed; Brady Christensen is doing well and could be in the mix. Carolina has extra days to prepare for the Broncos.

injuries.detail: Hamstring injury. Canales said the team will know more about the timeline shortly and does not yet know whether he is an IR candidate.
A reporter said he went down with an injury. Canales did not give a specific update, only that the team is evaluating the line.

signals.claim: The offense will look for a more balanced, rhythmic pass game with quicker timing and cleaner protection at the snap to give Young time.
signals.note: Opponents are taking away the vertical shots and protection is shaky, so Young's deep-ball upside is uncertain while quicker throws could raise his floor.

signals.claim: Lee has a hamstring injury, and the team will have a clearer timeline soon, including whether he goes on IR.
signals.note: The CB depth is thin, which could mean pressure on the Panthers' pass defense.

Canales said the urgency comes from himself and the staff, not from ownership. He said the offense is held to the same standard and that the firings were not about offensive struggles.

title: Brian Schottenheimer on 105.3 The Fan | 10-30-26
headline: Cowboys are committed to run/pass balance after the Eagles win; Tyler Smith's return is helping the OL, and the defense is getting healthier (Demo back, Joey Porter Jr. now comfortable) ahead of Arizona and Trey McBride.
summary: Schottenheimer said the offense played with much more balance against Philadelphia after the running game stalled in the Tampa and Green Bay losses, and he wants to hurt teams both running and throwing. He credited the offensive line's best game of the season to Tyler Smith's return and the group playing together, noting they were physically dominant against a strong Eagles front. He defended play calls like runs on third-and-long and in the red zone, saying Dak Prescott totally understands and he has more confidence in Dak than anyone. He explained the end-of-half timeout sequence, saying the team wants to stay on the ball and snap in the 28-32 second range but was a bit slow on the double move to CeeDee Lamb. On defense he called the unit inconsistent but pointed to a strong second half and to improving health as the big reason for optimism. He singled out Joey Porter Jr. as finally comfortable in the system, DeMarvion Overshown's return as huge, Shemar James playing great, and Quinnen Williams playing like himself. For Arizona, he praised Budda Baker and the multiple three-safety looks of Nick Rallis' defense, called Trey McBride dynamic and the focal point of the offense, and said ball security will decide the game given Dallas is 1-8 in the last nine against the Cardinals.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: “The Ball Is What This Game Comes Down To” | Press Conference
headline: Shemar James has locked in as the Cowboys' middle linebacker, while Dee Winters is likely out another week and Luke Schoonmaker is a late-week check.
summary: Schottenheimer said Shemar James has earned the middle linebacker job, praising his command and calming influence on the defense. He described the linebacker spot as a rotation by nature, with Jaishawn Barham and DeMarvion Overshown cross-trained and playing different packages based on formation and call. He said Dee Winters will be hard to get back this week and is probably a week away. He called Pickens, Quinnen Williams and Caleb Downs healthy enough to play, and said Luke Schoonmaker is fine but he wants to see how he moves at practice. On Arizona, he said turnovers, not energy, are the reason the Cowboys have lost four straight at home, pointing to an 11-turnover deficit in those games. He said the defense is ready for Arizona's disguised blitzes, and that the offense must get Trey McBride boxed in because the ball will go his way. He credited the offensive line and tight ends for consistent run blocking and gave game balls to the line, including Broderick Jones. He also said a roster decision would come after practice.

title: HC Sean Payton on Week 8 vs. Chiefs: ‘It’s a divisional game, and those are important’
headline: Payton gave little actionable injury news: RJ Harvey has 'no status' for now, the backfield stays a deep three-back rotation with J.K. Dobbins doing well, and Denver prepares for a divisional Week 8 game against the Chiefs.
summary: Payton was asked whether Dobbins is on a load-management plan. He said three backs make it harder to balance touches than two, that Dobbins is doing well, and that the room is deep and he likes how they play. He added that Dobbins' analytical numbers (burst and speed) have peaked. Asked about RJ Harvey's status, he said only 'No status right now.' On spreading the ball around, he said he talks often with pass catchers about their targets, installs plays so certain players see looks, and a hot-hand element exists but is easier to apply at running back than at receiver. He explained that jumbo packages are game-plan dependent, used to force a defense into its base personnel for runs designed against base, and he mentioned Trautman and Engram as the tight ends who might otherwise draw sub packages. He said red-zone defense starts with stopping the run and winning third down. He called the Chiefs game an important divisional game and said Denver doesn't compartmentalize the season into quarters. He wants better pursuit to the ball against the run than in Week 1, and he praised kicker Will Lutz's consistency and playoff experience. The rest was reminiscing about scouting Patrick Mahomes and admiration for the Chiefs' creativity.

signals.claim: Dobbins will remain part of a three-back rotation rather than get a clear lead role; no load-management plan was confirmed.

title: Campbell on Minnesota Vikings
headline: Brian Branch has no limitations against Minnesota, and Cade Mays gets a second week back. Isiah Pacheco could return in mid-to-late December.
summary: Campbell said Brian Branch is in a good place after playing every defensive snap in the second half last week. He called the volume "perfect" and said Branch has no limitations against Minnesota. Safety Kerby Joseph is being brought back slowly: he has done only individual and group work, with no team reps yet. The plan is for him to be in real practice next week, and the sleeve he wore was just a normal way to manage swelling. Campbell praised Jahmyr Gibbs as a complete back who takes everything personally and keeps improving, including in pass protection. He said Minnesota's blitz-heavy, man-coverage defense will test the tackles, guards, Cade Mays and the backs, and that running the ball well will be critical. Mays is back for a second week and took more reps than Branch did, which Campbell expects to help his conditioning. Isiah Pacheco is progressing well, with a chance to return in mid-to-late December. Devin White is "doing pretty good," and Thomas Harper is close to ready but being handled cautiously. On the trade deadline, Campbell said the front office is working daily, and the Germany trip won't affect it.

Running the ball well on early downs is the key, and the team must handle pressures and finish downfield.
Campbell called Dallas Turner a strong run defender and pass rusher who has taken another step this year. He said Blake Miller and Penei Sewell have their hands full but will be ready.
The front office is working on trades every day, and Campbell said the Germany trip and time difference won't affect any deal.
Minnesota is 2-0 in the division. A win would put Detroit in position to stay in the hunt, and Campbell wants clean, disciplined football for four quarters.

title: Matt LaFleur likes 'the aggressive style' defense showed against Panthers
headline: Packers' run game is a real problem (LaFleur: 'not a lot' to be optimistic about), so Jordan Love's arm carries the offense; Christian Watson returned after an ambulance scare and Ty'Ron Hopper starred on defense.
summary: LaFleur praised the defense for its aggressive, pressure-heavy performance in the 27-19 Thursday night win over Carolina, which led the league in explosive passes but was held in check. He singled out Ty'Ron Hopper for a huge night and credited defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon and the staff, noting six players each had a sack. On offense he was blunt that the run game has been ineffective, including a failed attempt to run out the clock late, and said he sees little reason for optimism right now even though pass protection has improved. The offensive line was reshuffled: John Williams played center, Larkin moved to right guard, and Aaron Banks returned, with Kevin Zeitler on the bench but still trusted. Christian Watson was taken away in an ambulance after landing on the ball and coughing up blood, cleared a CT scan, and went back into the game and played well. LaFleur defended Jordan Love, saying he carries the burden of the offense and was good apart from a late interception, and explained that many quick throws came from Carolina's scheme. J. Michael Sturdivant made a notable catch, and LaFleur backed returner Coleman Owen after a fumble on the opening kickoff, refusing to pull him. He also said the team overcame losing the turnover battle by two.

title: Shane Steichen: Week 8 final update, Colts at Jaguars
headline: Josh Downs (reported trade request) and Jonathan Taylor are both set to play Sunday at Jacksonville, Tyler Warren is good to go, and rookie RB Seth McGowan's role is set to keep growing against the league's top run defense.
summary: Steichen opened by ruling out Anthony Gould and Justin Walley, and said Tyler Warren and Sauce Gardner are good to go for Sunday. He confirmed that Josh (almost certainly Josh Downs), who reportedly requested a trade, practiced this week and will play his normal snaps. He said he had private conversations with the player, told him to be a professional, and expects him at his best. He gave the same answer for Jonathan Taylor, whom he also praised for stepping up as a leader after the team lost two of its leaders. Steichen called Jacksonville's run defense gap sound, physical, and well-coached, with varied fronts and pressure packages. Asked about McGowan's recent uptick in carries, he said the team will keep integrating the physical rookie, citing his juice and growth. He was also upbeat about Jalen Farmer, praising his physicality, energy, and growth in communication and pass protection, and said he is looking forward to seeing him play. Steichen framed the game as a chance to get within reach of the division lead, with the team one game out and ten left.

title: Liam Coen Reviews Strong Week of Practice, Talks Game Plan for Colts | Press Conference
headline: Chris Rodriguez Jr. is earning more trust, including in pass protection, and Coen hopes to need him against the Colts in a wet, windy game; Emmanuel Pregnon is progressing as a rookie OL.
summary: Coen said the Jaguars had their best practice in a long time on Thursday after the bye, with Wednesday also physical. The game plan for the Colts is finished. Saturday will focus on situational football, and Coen expects wind and rain to affect the game, so the team drilled wet-ball work all week. He said the wet ball is more of a concern for pass catchers than for Trevor Lawrence, who has big hands and threw well in the rain last year. He praised Chris Rodriguez Jr., saying he has shown more trust in pass protection and in understanding his role beyond first and second down, and he hopes to need him Sunday given the expected game type. He praised rookie guard Emmanuel Pregnon as a physical people mover who is improving in pass protection, with room to grow at the second level. He praised Kaevon Merriweather for stepping in amid injuries. On the Colts, Coen called them a very well-coached team and said injuries to their nickel defenders make their defensive approach hard to predict. He also said he doesn't game plan the following Thursday night opponent ahead of time.

injuries.detail: Coen said Merriweather has stepped in because of injuries in the secondary. He did not give a specific injury designation or name who is hurt.

signals.claim: Rodriguez will be trusted in pass-protection and passing-down situations and is expected to be needed in the run game Sunday against the Colts.
signals.note: Earning pass-down trust broadens his role beyond early-down running, and a wet, windy game script could favor rushing volume.

signals.claim: Pregnon will keep starting at offensive line as a rookie while developing his blocking at the second level.
signals.note: A physical run blocker improving in pass protection is mildly good for the Jaguars' run game and pass protection.

signals.claim: Lawrence is not expected to be hurt much by wet conditions Sunday.
signals.note: Wet, windy weather could limit the passing game overall, but Coen has little concern about Lawrence's ball security.
signals.quote: Trevor threw it really good last time in the rain specifically.

signals.claim: Merriweather will continue to fill in at safety while the team deals with injuries.
signals.note: Mainly relevant to IDP leagues, as he is playing a larger defensive role.
signals.quote: he's done a nice job stepping in for us.

topics.detail: The offense practiced with wet balls on Wednesday and Thursday, focusing on ball security, routes on air and hand use. Coen expects wind and rain Sunday, and said pass catchers' focus on their hands is a big part of the game plan.
The post-bye practices were energetic, with Thursday described as their best in a long time. The game plan is about 99% done, and Saturday will focus on situational football.

Coen called the Colts well coached in all three phases, with good run schemes, offensive line and tight ends. Their nickel injuries make their defensive approach hard to predict, and he expects a mix of protecting and pressuring.

Coen has not looked ahead to the Thursday night opponent because as a play caller he can't game plan two opponents at once. Assistants did background work during the bye, and he expects carryover from earlier game plans.

title: Andy Reid on Broncos: 'Two Good Football Teams That Have a Chance to Play Each Other' | Press Conference 10/30

summary: Reid opened with the injury report. Rookie corner Mansoor Delane did not practice, and Reid confirmed it is the same shoulder issue as before. R Mason Thomas was away from the team for personal reasons, but Reid said he will meet the team in Denver and expects him to play. Asked if he was optimistic that Rashee Rice would be available, Reid answered with a quick, positive yes. Reid called Denver a good team in a great atmosphere and said the team had a good week of practice. He confirmed the kicker for the weekend will be Harrison. He described Denver's returning player, who is coming off the commissioner's list, as an energetic, Pro Bowl-caliber player. He framed the game as two good AFC West teams playing each other and played down any extra significance from the standings.

title: Sean McVay breaks down the Week 8 injury report, what he expects on Sunday vs. the Chargers & more
headline: Rams injury report: Coleman Shelton (hip), Colby Parkinson and Trent McDuffie (groin) all questionable vs. Chargers, and Jordan Whittington is back but questionable. Dylan McMahon is ready to step in at center.
summary: McVay opened with the injury report. Coleman Shelton was limited and is questionable with a hip issue. Colby Parkinson did not practice and is questionable. Long snapper Joe Cardona is doubtful with an ankle, so Jake McQuade would step in. Trent McDuffie was limited and is questionable with a groin issue, with McVay hopeful but still monitoring. Jordan Whittington's injury locked up within the last 30 minutes, and McVay called him tough, listing him as questionable. If Shelton can't go, Dylan McMahon would start at center. McMahon got plenty of work this week because of how Shelton has been managed. McVay praised the defense's physicality, situational play and red-zone stops over the last two weeks. He said last week's offense worked because of efficiency on early downs, which set up play action. He also said the absence of top playmakers changes personnel groupings, but other players have stepped up, including tight ends, both running backs and receivers, while Puka Nacua will still get his share.

The absence of key playmakers changes personnel groupings, but other players are stepping up, including tight ends, both running backs and receivers.

title: Jim Harbaugh on Players Returning From Injury Ahead of Rams Matchup
headline: Harbaugh was vague on who returns this week; two unnamed players with setbacks (a hamstring on top of a quad injury) are both out Sunday vs. the Rams.
summary: Harbaugh spoke after the bye week and said the team is feeling good about its preparation and is in a good place heading into the Rams game. He was glad to have some players back from injury and said a player (name garbled in the captions) was not even on the injury report. Asked whether a specific player would settle in at right tackle, he declined to say who would line up on Sunday. He described Matthew Stafford as one of the best and said stopping him takes connected play at all three levels of the defense, since Stafford can get the ball to every part of the field. On the mental side, he said he does not worry and the team's approach is simply to work and not worry. Near the end he said one player had a setback in rehab, and a follow-up question indicated a hamstring injury on top of a quad problem. He said he knew that both players he was asked about are out for Sunday. The captions never make clear which players he meant, so no injury is attributed to a named player.

title: Klint Kubiak lists JPJ as questionable for Jets matchup
headline: JJ (likely Jack Bech? unclear) is questionable and Patrick Johnson is out for Week 8 vs. the Jets; Trey (likely Trey Zuhn) could see OL snaps, and Jalen Nailor is expected to make plays with Kirk Cousins.
summary: Kubiak opened by saying JJ is questionable and Patrick Johnson is out for Sunday's game against the Jets. He gave no firm answers on roster elevations or activations, saying the team has until tomorrow to decide on a possible activation and that a practice-squad elevation to replace Johnson would be decided then. He said Dante's playing time is still to be determined. He named Ashton, Maxx and Dylan as captains, calling it a body of work, and praised Maxx Crosby's preparation and leadership. On the passing game, he said Jalen Nailor is expected to make plays and that the connection with Kirk Cousins needs time on task, with receivers getting open and Cousins going through his progressions. He praised Tre Tucker's conditioning, said starting NFL receivers must be able to play about 70 plays at full speed, and noted he has stood out since April. On the offensive line, Trey has battled back from an injury and could play Sunday. He gave general answers on the run defense, saying it is team defense, and on the run game, saying the offense just needs to perform, and he praised Nakobe Dean as the defensive leader who will be given more responsibility as he produces.

title: Kevin O’Connell on the Run Game & Preparing for Vikings vs. Lions Matchup in Detroit
headline: Jordan Mason is set to be a focal point of the Vikings backfield, with Aaron Jones still in a significant role but dealing with a knee issue that flared up. Jay Ward is the only player listed questionable for Detroit.
summary: O'Connell said Jay Ward is the team's only questionable player for the Week 8 game at Detroit. Ward had knee soreness, was limited in practice, and is expected to play. Everyone else either practiced fully or had a planned rest day. On the backfield, last week's Aaron Jones/Jordan Mason split was roughly 60-70 to 30. O'Connell said the staff wants Jordan to be a focal point and to get enough touches to get back in sync, while Jones keeps a significant role. Jones' knee flared up after the bye, possibly from a hit or going to the ground, and O'Connell expects him to put it behind him. He praised Detroit's defensive front, citing the edge rushers, interior depth, and the return of a key player. On Kyler Murray, he said the protect-the-ball conversation is mostly about play-calling risk. They still want to be aggressive in the pass game but ask Kyler to be smart and keep completing passes. He called rookie fullback Max Bredeson a trusted starter in 21 and 22 personnel who also contributes on special teams. He also praised returner Myles Price and called the NFC North the best division in football.

title: Head Coach Mike Vrabel 10/30: "Everybody comes in and prepares as a starter"
headline: A.J. Brown is questionable for the Week 9 trip to Miami after being unable to finish Wednesday's practice; with Romeo Doubs and Matt Pryor on IR, the WR room is thin, and TreVeyon Henderson is also questionable.
summary: Vrabel said A.J. Brown is questionable, and a decision will come after seeing how he is tomorrow. Brown could not finish practice on Wednesday, and the team is still treating him. Vrabel dodged a question about whether Brown was rushed back and said the two issues are separate. Asked about Brown's heavy snap load, he said the team wants its best players on the field and counts Brown as one of them. He listed TreVeyon Henderson and Christian Elliss as questionable too, calling them 'the usual suspects' and saying he did not want to misspeak. On Christian Barmore, he said the goal is to have him affect the quarterback as his primary role while finding roles for everyone. He declined to say whether Ben Brown's return to practice changes the guard plan, and he offered no strong theory on the rise in in-season trades.

title: Aaron Glenn Press Conference (10/30) | Week 8
headline: Breece Hall was limited again but is expected to be a key piece Sunday. T'Vondre Sweat, Joe Tippmann and Max Mitchell are out, and edge rusher David Bailey is doubtful against the Raiders.
summary: Glenn opened with the Friday injury report. Sweat, Joe (likely Tippmann) and Max Mitchell are out, and David Bailey is doubtful and will be a game-time decision. Breece Hall and Dylan Parham were limited, and Braelon Allen was full. Glenn said one player will be questionable, but the caption garbles the name. Asked why Hall has been limited for so long, he called Hall a key cog and said he has to hit certain checkpoints. Glenn said losing Sweat hurts because he wants a strong defensive middle with Sweat, Demario Davis and Minkah Fitzpatrick, but he trusts the depth behind them. If Bailey can't go, the remaining edge rushers will have to play more. He praised Darrell Jackson Jr.'s growth as he moves around the defensive line. He also said the tight end room has improved a lot, with 13 personnel used often and lots of mixing and matching. He previewed the Raiders by discussing Kirk Cousins, Maxx Crosby, setting the edge and Fernando Mendoza, and he deflected a question about comments from Ashton Jeanty.

topics.detail: Glenn said the tight end room has improved a lot since camp and the team plays plenty of 13 personnel. He said there is a lot of mixing and matching available, and often four tight ends are active.
After Miami got the edge on them last week, Glenn called setting the edge the basis of the defense. He wants outside runs forced inside to the big interior linemen.
Glenn said Cousins processes very well and has seen every kind of pressure. The plan is to disrupt the pocket and reroute receivers.

Glenn called Crosby relentless, long and instinctive, and said the Jets expect to see a lot of him. He said he talked to one of his players about matching up with Crosby, and that some help will be needed.

Asked about getting a player the ball more, Glenn said there is only one ball and many people need touches, including Garrett Wilson, Braelon Allen and Mason Taylor. He said they must find ways to get that player involved, but others can make plays too.

Two players on IR (Yamada and McCrary, per the question) are planned to return as rehab allows. Glenn praised Fernando Mendoza's toughness and leadership and said he doesn't know whether Mendoza will play.

title: Nick Sirianni Press Conference: October 30, 2026
headline: Saquon Barkley's availability for Sunday night is still unresolved (Sirianni: 'we'll see'), with Elijah Mitchell and Jaydon Blue set to carry the RB load if he sits.
summary: Sirianni spent much of the session on process. He said 'what happens Monday to Saturday is usually what happens Sunday' and that the team's detail has to improve, while insisting nobody is slacking in effort. Asked whether Saquon Barkley can play this week, he did not commit and said they would see at the end of the week. He said he feels good about the RB room's depth even though it has been hit hard by injuries. He singled out Elijah Mitchell, who is back after getting dinged up in camp, and Jaydon Blue as the backs ready to step in. On leadership, he praised Barkley, Jordan Davis, Jordan Mailata, Cooper DeJean, Quinyon Mitchell, Dallas Goedert and Landon Dickerson, and noted that DeVonta Smith has been banged up. He said trade-deadline talks with Howie Roseman follow the same process as in past years, regardless of record. He called the run game a group staff effort. He also said pass protection is always important, and the team will need to be technically sound against Washington's pressure and confusion looks.

injuries.detail: Sirianni wouldn't say whether he plays Sunday; 'we'll see' at the end of the week. The RB room is described as beat up.

topics.detail: Sirianni said the team's detail must improve across the board and that focus in meetings and practice drives results. He said he is 'results aware' but 'process driven' and denied any effort problem.
With several elected captains injured, he pointed to healthy veterans like Barkley, Mailata, Jordan Davis, DeJean, Mitchell, Goedert and Dickerson. He named Nolan Smith as a future leader.
He said conversations with Howie Roseman about buying or selling are the same as in his first five years, driven by consistent process regardless of record. He gave no hints about specific moves.
He declined to name one coach who leads the run game and called it a group staff effort, as with the pass game and protections.

He said pass pro matters more against an aggressive defense that creates confusion. He stressed avoiding technical errors on stunts and with free runners. Protection is always the first meeting of the week.

title: Robert Saleh Press Conference | Tennessee Titans
headline: Rookie WR Carnell Tate (shoulder) and a player Saleh called 'Taj' (likely Tyjae Spears) are in doubt for the game, Jeffery Simmons is gone, and Alontae Taylor is close to returning at nickel.
summary: Saleh opened by saying three players, which the captions render as 'Taj,' Tate and Townsend, did not practice Friday and have their status 'in doubt.' He was unsure whether that meant an official 'doubtful' tag. On Tate, he said missing a full week of practice is complicated for a young player. The team would work him out Friday to push the injury and see how he responds. He said the injury likely happened on the fumble, when the player landed on his shoulder, and he did not feel it until the next morning. On defense, Saleh said the team will not blitz more just because Jeffery Simmons is gone. Pressure varies by game, and the opponent's elite skill players mean extra blitzers create more one-on-ones in the back end. He is open to different packages, including dime, five or seven DBs, and possibly a three-lineman front. Alontae Taylor had a great week of practice, showed physicality in pads, and is 'getting closer' to playing. He still has to take the nickel job from Marcus Harris, who has been playing well. Saleh also said another player earned more snaps last week and the staff is looking for the best three defensive backs. On Cam Ward, Saleh said the goal is getting him better every day rather than making him the face of the franchise.
